# The *Other* Game-Changers {.section-title background-color="#12132A"}

[2:05–2:45 · four systems that aren't LLMs]{.muted}

::: notes
Frame the section: "Each of these is a totally different stack. Different
math, different shape, different training. By the end I want you to feel the
*variety* under the AI umbrella, not just the LLM corner."
:::

## AlphaGo — hook {.smaller}

> **The metaphor.** A chess player who plays themselves a million times
> overnight, and wakes up smarter than they were.

[2016: beat the world's best Go player a decade before anyone expected.]{.muted}

::: notes
Hook only. Sell the *image* before any technical detail. Pause on "wakes up
smarter than they were" — it does the work of the whole module.
:::

## AlphaGo — mechanism {.smaller}

- **Monte Carlo Tree Search** — imagine playing out a position a thousand times in your head, randomly, and keeping score
- **Policy network** — narrows the imagined moves to the ones a strong player would consider
- **Value network** — guesses who's winning, without playing out the rest
- **Self-play** — the engine is its own training partner, getting harder every iteration

::: notes
Each bullet is the metaphor first, then the technical name. "Imagine playing
out…" → "that's MCTS." Don't apologize for skipping the math; just name it.
AlphaZero generalized this; MuZero learned the rules from scratch.
:::

## AlphaGo — why it matters {.smaller}

- Go was the **canonical "computers can't do this"** game — too intuitive for brute force
- Killed it a decade early
- The recipe (search + learned policy/value + self-play) **is now load-bearing across reasoning AI**
- Modern LLM "thinking" modes are quietly running cousins of this loop

::: notes
The point of this slide isn't AlphaGo. It's that the *recipe* — search +
guidance — keeps showing up. Land that and you've set up the bridge slide.
:::

## AlphaGo — further reading {.smaller}

- Silver et al., *Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search* — [Nature 2016](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature16961)
- Silver et al., *Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play* (AlphaZero) — [arXiv:1712.01815](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.01815)
- Schrittwieser et al., *Mastering Atari, Go, chess and shogi by planning with a learned model* (MuZero) — [Nature 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-03051-4)
- DeepMind retrospective documentary — *AlphaGo* (2017)

## AlphaFold — hook {.smaller}

> **The metaphor.** Origami, but the paper is a sentence of amino acids and
> the final shape decides whether the protein heals you or kills you.

[2020: cracked a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology.]{.muted}

::: notes
Audience may not know what a protein is doing. Ground them: "everything in
your body is proteins folding into shapes; the shape *is* the function."
:::

## AlphaFold — mechanism {.smaller}

- **Input:** the amino acid sequence + a search through known related proteins
- **Evoformer:** a transformer that reasons about which positions are talking to each other
- **Structure module:** a *geometry-aware* network that respects rotations and translations — turn the molecule, the prediction turns with it
- **Output:** atom coordinates good enough for drug discovery

::: notes
The trick is the *geometric* / equivariant bit — the math respects physical
symmetry instead of memorizing it. That's why it generalizes.
:::

## AlphaFold — why it matters {.smaller}

- Structures for **nearly every known protein**, free online
- 2024 **Nobel Prize in Chemistry**
- Drug discovery, enzyme engineering, materials science — all changed timelines
- And the architecture is **transformers + GNN + geometry** stacked — *not just one trick*

## AlphaFold — further reading {.smaller}

- Jumper et al., *Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold* — [Nature 2021](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-021-03819-2)
- AlphaFold Protein Structure Database — [alphafold.ebi.ac.uk](https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/)
- DeepMind's *AlphaFold 3* announcement — [blog](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/alphafold-3-predicts-the-structure-and-interactions-of-all-of-lifes-molecules/)
- Mohammed AlQuraishi, *AlphaFold at CASP13* — accessible deep dive on the architecture

## Stable Diffusion — hook {.smaller}

> **The metaphor.** Start with TV static. Squint at it until you see a cat.
> Squint harder, and the cat sharpens. The model is the trained squint.

[2022: image generation went from "research toy" to a phone app.]{.muted}

::: notes
This is the moment the audience leans in — they've all used these tools but
nobody told them what's happening under the hood.
:::

## Stable Diffusion — mechanism {.smaller}

- **Forward process:** take an image and add noise, step by step, until it's pure static
- **Reverse process:** train a network to undo *one step* of noise at a time
- **At generation:** start from static, run the network many times, end with an image
- **Text conditioning:** at each step, also tell the network what to denoise toward ("a cat in a spacesuit")

[Generation is **denoising**, not prediction. A different paradigm wearing a familiar product.]{.accent-magenta}

::: notes
Name the math: this is a "score-based" or "diffusion" model, mathematically
close to physics — Langevin dynamics, energy landscapes. Tee up energy-based
models in §2.
:::

## Stable Diffusion — why it matters {.smaller}

- The first paradigm shift in generative modeling since GANs
- Generalized to **video, audio, 3D, protein backbones** (RFdiffusion)
- The math is **stochastic differential equations**, not next-token prediction
- LLMs aren't the only frontier — energy-based generation is its own arc

## Stable Diffusion — further reading {.smaller}

- Ho et al., *Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models* (DDPM) — [arXiv:2006.11239](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239)
- Rombach et al., *High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models* (Stable Diffusion) — [arXiv:2112.10752](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10752)
- Yang Song, *Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution* — [blog](https://yang-song.net/blog/2021/score/)
- Lilian Weng, *What are Diffusion Models?* — [blog](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2021-07-11-diffusion-models/)

## AlphaProof / AlphaGeometry — hook {.smaller}

> **The metaphor.** Pair-programming with a mathematician — one half guesses,
> the other half proves. Guess fast, check slow.

[2024: silver-medal level on the International Math Olympiad.]{.muted}

::: notes
This is *the* concrete neurosymbolic story. Lean on the pair-programming
image — most of the room has done it.
:::

## AlphaProof / AlphaGeometry — mechanism {.smaller}

- **Neural side:** generates candidate steps — fast, creative, sometimes wrong
- **Symbolic side:** a *formal verifier* (Lean, or a custom geometry engine) — slow, exact, always right
- The two **trade hand-offs**: neural proposes, symbolic accepts or rejects, neural learns from the verdict

[Pattern-matching **+** provable correctness. Neither alone is enough.]{.accent-magenta}

::: notes
Olympiad geometry is solved by AlphaGeometry; algebra/number-theory by
AlphaProof talking to Lean. The general principle: pair a fast learner with
a slow checker.
:::

## AlphaProof / AlphaGeometry — why it matters {.smaller}

- IMO problems are where you **cannot bluff** — the answer has to be provable
- First serious demonstration of **neurosymbolic AI at frontier capability**
- A different shape of "intelligent": **search guided by formal proof**, not just next-token guess
- Sets up the neurosymbolic paradigm in the next section

## AlphaProof / AlphaGeometry — further reading {.smaller}

- DeepMind, *AI achieves silver-medal standard solving International Mathematical Olympiad problems* — [blog](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/ai-solves-imo-problems-at-silver-medal-level/)
- Trinh et al., *Solving olympiad geometry without human demonstrations* (AlphaGeometry) — [Nature 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06747-5)
- Lean theorem prover — [leanprover.github.io](https://leanprover.github.io/)
- Terence Tao's [first-impressions blog post](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/) on the IMO result

---

## Stacks, not tricks {.smaller}

Every system we just walked through is **multiple paradigms stacked**:

- AlphaGo = MCTS + deep RL + self-play
- AlphaFold = transformers + GNN + geometric deep learning
- Stable Diffusion = score-based / diffusion + U-Net + text conditioning
- AlphaProof = neural search + symbolic verifier

[So: let's look at the paradigms themselves.]{.accent-magenta}

::: notes
This is the bridge. Hold it for a beat. The audience now has the *motivation*
to care about Section 2 — they've seen these paradigms in action.
:::

# Paradigms Beyond LLMs {.section-title background-color="#12132A"}

[3:00–3:45 · three families + honorable mentions]{.muted}

## Evolutionary methods — hook {.smaller}

> **The metaphor.** Throw a thousand random solutions at the wall. Keep the
> ones that stick. Mash them together. Repeat for a few thousand generations.
> Survival pressure does the rest.

[No gradients. No backprop. Just selection.]{.muted}

## Evolutionary methods — mechanism {.smaller}

- **Population** of candidate solutions (weights, programs, architectures, behaviors)
- **Fitness function** scores each one
- **Selection · mutation · recombination** produce the next generation
- Variants: **GA** (bits), **ES / CMA-ES** (continuous, with adaptive step size), **NEAT** (evolves *topology*), **GP** (evolves *programs*), **swarm** (collective behavior)

[Embarrassingly parallel. Works on black-box, discrete, non-differentiable problems where SGD can't go.]{.accent-magenta}

## Evolutionary methods — why it matters {.smaller}

- Architecture and hyperparameter search
- Robotics controllers when reward is sparse
- **OpenAI showed ES competitive with deep RL** on Atari (2017)
- Antenna design, circuit design, scheduling — anywhere you can recognize a good answer but can't write its derivative
- The substrate for the **deep dive coming up at 3:50**

## Evolutionary methods — further reading {.smaller}

- Salimans et al., *Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning* — [arXiv:1703.03864](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.03864)
- Hansen, *The CMA Evolution Strategy: A Tutorial* — [arXiv:1604.00772](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.00772)
- Stanley & Miikkulainen, *NEAT* — [original paper](https://nn.cs.utexas.edu/?stanley:ec02)
- Koza, *Genetic Programming* (book) — the canonical reference

## Energy-based models — hook {.smaller}

> **The metaphor.** A landscape of hills and valleys. Drop a marble anywhere.
> It rolls downhill. The valleys are the things the model thinks are *real*.

[Train the landscape; let physics handle generation.]{.muted}

## Energy-based models — mechanism {.smaller}

- Define an **energy function** over configurations — lower energy means more "right"
- **Training** lowers the energy of real data, raises it for everything else
- **Generation** is rolling downhill: start somewhere random, follow the gradient of the landscape
- **Diffusion models** are a special case — they learn the local slope of the landscape (the *score*)

[Hopfield networks (associative memory) won the **2024 Nobel Prize in Physics**.]{.accent-amber}

::: notes
This is the connective tissue: stable diffusion in Section 1 *is* an energy-based
model. Hopfield is the historical anchor. Score-based and diffusion are the
modern flagship.
:::

## Energy-based models — why it matters {.smaller}

- The math is **physics**, not linguistics — different intuitions, different limits
- Generative modeling for images, video, audio, 3D, protein backbones
- Associative memory: store patterns, recall from corrupted inputs
- A different theory of "what does it mean for a model to know something"

## Energy-based models — further reading {.smaller}

- LeCun, *A Tutorial on Energy-Based Learning* — [PDF](https://yann.lecun.com/exdb/publis/pdf/lecun-06.pdf)
- Hopfield, *Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities* (1982) — Nobel-cited
- Song & Ermon, *Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution* — [NeurIPS 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.05600)
- Hoogeboom et al., *Equivariant Diffusion for Molecule Generation* — [arXiv:2203.17003](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.17003)

## Neurosymbolic AI — hook {.smaller}

> **The metaphor.** A musician who can also read sheet music. The ear catches
> what's there; the page catches what *has* to be there.

[Perception **+** logic. Intuition **+** proof.]{.muted}

## Neurosymbolic AI — mechanism {.smaller}

- **Neural** front-ends do perception, pattern-matching, fuzzy reasoning
- **Symbolic** back-ends do logic, composition, verifiable correctness
- Architectures vary widely: neural-then-symbolic pipelines, differentiable logic, program synthesis with neural priors, **LLM + formal verifier** (AlphaProof)
- Bet: **pure pattern-matching hits a ceiling; pure logic hits a ceiling; the interesting space is between**

## Neurosymbolic AI — why it matters {.smaller}

- Theorem proving (AlphaProof, LeanDojo)
- Program synthesis
- Scientific discovery
- Anywhere you need **both** perception and verifiable correctness — autonomy, law, medicine, math
- The most likely shape of "intelligence" past raw scaling

## Neurosymbolic AI — further reading {.smaller}

- Garcez & Lamb, *Neurosymbolic AI: The 3rd Wave* — [arXiv:2012.05876](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.05876)
- Kautz, *The Third AI Summer* — [AAAI talk](https://henrykautz.com/talks/)
- Mao et al., *The Neuro-Symbolic Concept Learner* — [ICLR 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12584)
- LeanDojo — [leandojo.org](https://leandojo.org/)

## Honorable mentions {.smaller}

- **Gradient-boosted trees** (XGBoost, LightGBM) — still king of tabular data · [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.02754)
- **Probabilistic / Bayesian methods** — when calibrated uncertainty matters more than raw accuracy
- **Geometric DL & GNNs** — AlphaFold, weather (GraphCast), materials science
- **State-space models** (Mamba, S4) — linear-time challenger to transformers · [Mamba](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00752)
- **Active inference / Free energy** — perception and action as one optimization · increasingly relevant to consciousness research
- **Cellular automata / Neural CA** — emergence from local rules · [growing NCA](https://distill.pub/2020/growing-ca/)
- **Spiking / neuromorphic** — ultra-low-power biological-style nets on specialized hardware

[Further reading lives in the repo's `references.bib` — full citations, click through.]{.muted .footer}

# Research Deep Dive {.section-title background-color="#12132A"}

[3:50–4:30 · hierarchical evolutionary systems with orchestration]{.muted}

## Why hierarchy, why evolution, why orchestration {.smaller}

- **Why evolution** — gradients require a smooth, differentiable objective. Most interesting objectives aren't.
- **Why hierarchy** — search at a single scale plateaus. Stack search inside search and the plateau breaks.
- **Why orchestration at the top** — the upper layer's job isn't to *solve* — it's to *decide which layer below is solving the right problem*

[The thesis: **stacked search, glued together by something that can reason about the stack itself.**]{.accent-magenta}

::: notes
Don't rush this. The motivation sells the rest. If the room is with you on
*why*, the architecture diagram on the next slide does the rest of the work.
:::

## Architecture sketch {.smaller}

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph L0["L0 · Substrate"]
    P0["Population of solutions"]
    F0["Fitness eval"]
    P0 --> F0 --> P0
  end
  subgraph L1["L1 · Strategy"]
    P1["Population of L0 configurations"]
    F1["Meta-fitness"]
    P1 --> F1 --> P1
  end
  subgraph L2["L2 · Goal"]
    P2["Population of L1 objectives"]
    F2["Outer signal"]
    P2 --> F2 --> P2
  end
  ORCH(("Orchestrator")):::accent
  ORCH -. directs .-> L2
  ORCH -. directs .-> L1
  ORCH -. directs .-> L0
  L0 --> L1 --> L2 --> ORCH

  classDef accent fill:#9B5CFF,stroke:#FF4FCB,color:#08080F;
```

[Three rungs · an orchestrator that reads the stack and adjusts pressure.]{.muted}

::: notes
Walk the diagram bottom-up. Each rung is a full evolutionary loop. The
orchestrator is the load-bearing piece — it's what makes this an *AI system*
and not just nested optimization.
:::

## What's working {.smaller}

- The substrate-level loop runs and converges on toy problems
- The orchestrator-as-LLM-with-tools framing has been useful for **prototyping the upper layer cheaply**
- Mapping the architecture onto **consciousness research** — specifically self-models, predictive processing — is producing testable questions

[Honest: this is a research program, not a product. Yet.]{.muted}

## What's open {.smaller}

- **Credit assignment across layers** — when the outer signal fires, which rung deserves the update?
- **Compute** — naively, hierarchy multiplies population × generations. Need shortcuts.
- **Evaluation** — what does "working" mean for a system whose objective is generated by another part of the same system?
- **Orchestrator stability** — the upper layer is the only non-evolutionary piece. Should it be?

## Where it touches consciousness research {.smaller}

- **Predictive processing** — agents that minimize a single quantity (free energy) look a lot like a hierarchy with an orchestrator
- **Active inference** — the Friston program; mathematically demanding, philosophically ambitious, increasingly relevant
- **Open-ended evolution** — does the system keep generating *novel* fitness regimes, or does it converge?
- The honest version: **we don't know what consciousness is**, but we have hypotheses with empirical hooks now

[I work on this part-time at Ardea. Augs is the planned product wrapper.]{.accent-cyan}

## Discussion prompts {.smaller}

1. Should the orchestrator itself be evolved, or is some non-evolutionary structure load-bearing?
2. Is hierarchy enough, or do we need **lateral** structure too (peer layers, not just stacked)?
3. Where does **active inference** belong in this picture — a fourth layer, or the *binding agent* across layers?
4. The honest one: how do we tell if this is **actually intelligent** vs. cleverly-engineered hill-climbing?

::: notes
Read them all up front, then pick whichever the room reacts to most. Prompt 4
is the one that usually surfaces the most interesting pushback.
:::
